title: OKR Threading & Initiative Ripple Plan for 2026 Q3-Q4
creator: Priya Menon
description: Summary: Create a repeatable playbook and artifact set to thread company-level OKRs down into initiative commitments across Product, Eng, Design, Research, and Growth for the remainder of 2026. Deliverables: 1) Initiative Dependency & Ripple Matrix (consolidated CSV + Confluence template), 2) Cross-functional cadence calendar (quarterly planning + monthly sync + weekly escalation), 3) Automation to surface blocker signals in the Console (dashboard + Linear labels mapping), 4) Updated PRD template fields for OKR traceability. Background: Past quarters saw misaligned rollouts where feature A (runtime kernel change) shipped ahead of rollout gating, which caused regression alerts and increased cost. The goal is to reduce those incidents by improving visibility and explicit dependencies when launching initiatives tied to company OKRs. Success metrics: - 50% reduction in cross-team unannounced dependency blockers during planning (measured via Linear labels and meeting notes) - 90% of initiatives with a single source-of-truth mapping to at least one company OKR by the start of the quarter - Time-to-resolution for cross-team blockers improves by 30% (Console incident dashboard) Approach: - Run a two-week pilot with three initiative owners (Runtime Performance, Dedicated Autoscaling, Console UX) to validate the matrix and cadence. - Use a lightweight artifact: a single-row-per-initiative CSV with fields: initiative_key, owner, linked_OKRs, upstream_deps, downstream_risks, rollout_guardrails, canary_policy, expected_metrics. - Align PD/Design/Eng owners in a "ripple review" session that annotates timelines and rollback/fallback plans. - Introduce a Linear automation that tags any issue with dependencies not assigned after 3 business days as "needs-owner" and pages the PM on-call. Trade-offs considered: - Heavy governance vs. lightweight nudges: we chose a lightweight matrix + automation to avoid blocking velocity at the cost of requiring more human follow-up in some complex launches. - Centralized vs. federated ownership: we keep initiative owners accountable and Product as the arbiter of the OKR mapping instead of a central committee to maintain speed. Stakeholders: - VP Product (Katherine Yu) - Head of Infra (Marco Liu) - Head of Platform (Anika Rao) - Head of Design (Samir Khan) - Head of Growth (Leah Ortiz) Risks & Mitigations: - Risk: teams treat the matrix as overhead. Mitigation: surface only initiative entries with active releases in the next 90 days and provide templates + reuse from previous quarters. - Risk: mismatch in metric definitions. Mitigation: require a short metric spec row and link to dashboard queries (Console) before the initiative is marked as "committed". Next steps: 1) Build Confluence template and CSV schema (owner: Evan) 2) Run pilot with the three initiatives (owners: Marcus Chen, Lina Ortega, Diego Perez) 3) Ship Linear automation rule and add Console dashboard panels (collab with Eng Observability)
comments: 2026-01-27 - Kickoff: ran initial framing with Katherine and Marco. Agreement on pilot scope (Runtime Perf, Dedicated Autoscaling, Console UX). Action: Evan to draft Confluence template by Feb 3.
2026-02-03 - Template v0.1 posted to Confluence (link above). Quick feedback from Design: add a 'UX rollout gating' field. Added this to the CSV schema.

2026-02-09 - Pilot kickoff with initiative owners. Noted inconsistent definitions for 'severity' in rollback criteria. Decision: require a one-line rollback SLA and an owner-assigned runbook link for all initiatives with production impact.
2026-02-18 - Eng suggested integrating the matrix with our service catalog to auto-populate upstream_deps for infra-owned services. Feasibility OK; added as follow-up (dependency: ENG-2213).

2026-02-22 - Small trade-off discussion: Heavy gating would slow launches. Consensus: use 'soft gates' — automated tagging + PM review, escalate only for high customer impact. Marked 'customer_impact' flag as required on commit.

2026-02-28 - Built a first Linear automation prototype: issues without an assigned dependency after 3 business days get tagged 'needs-owner' and the PM receives an @mention. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/linear-automation/pull/22

2026-03-03 - Pilot retrospective: Runtime Perf and Dedicated Autoscaling owners reported clearer timelines; Console UX requested better dashboard visibility into rollout progress. Action: Eng Observability to add two panels to the Console dashboard by Mar 18 (issue ENG-2337).
2026-03-05 - Decision: Roll the playbook company-wide for initiatives starting in Q3 with a run-in period of Q2 for templates and automation. Evan assigned to coordinate communications and training.
2026-03-05 - Open questions: how to reflect mid-quarter OKR shifts in the matrix? Proposal: tag affected initiatives with 'OKR-rebase' and require an updated mapping doc within 10 business days.
